query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Tuning the chemical composition of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be used to modify their magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
generation.material_initial_state: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy in a face-centered cubic (FCC) or body-centered cubic (BCC) crystalline structure
generation.intervention: Alloying with different elements to adjust the chemical composition
generation.conditions: Varied temperature and magnetic field conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Changes in the lattice parameter and atomic arrangement
generation.mechanism: Modification of the magnetic exchange interactions and spin fluctuations due to changes in the chemical composition and lattice parameter
generation.predicted_outcome: A change in the magnetocaloric effect (MCE) of up to 30% relative to the baseline MCE of the original alloy composition, measured in terms of the adiabatic temperature change (ΔT) in Kelvin
generation.baseline: The MCE of the original non-equiatomic HEA composition
generation.boundary: The Curie temperature (T_C) of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between the chemical composition, lattice parameter, and magnetic properties is complex and may involve additional factors such as grain size, defects, and impurities

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of the chemical composition of non-equiatomic HEAs and measurement of their magnetic and magnetocaloric properties
measurements: Magnetization vs. temperature and magnetic field
Adiabatic temperature change (ΔT) vs. magnetic field
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured MCE does not change by more than 5% relative to the baseline MCE for any given composition, the hypothesis is falsified
